item.title: Diabetes Access Widens as Travel and Privacy Shift
item.description: Medicine access, Wellington tracks, travel links, privacy changes and Australian reforms lead this recovery briefing.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh practical changes span medicine access, Wellington tracks, travel, transport rules, privacy and Australian consumer and health settings.

  1. Funded type 2 diabetes medicines widen from 1 September. Pharmac will broaden access to empagliflozin, empagliflozin with metformin, dulaglutide and liraglutide for people whose HbA1c remains above 53 mmol/mol despite other funded medicines, removing the current ethnicity, cardiovascular-risk and diabetic-kidney-disease criteria. Pharmac estimates about 14,000 additional people could benefit in the first year. 5 Aug 2026 decision; 1 Sep 2026 start. Source
  2. (Wellington hiking) Transmission Gully work has closed several Belmont tracks on weekdays. Greater Wellington’s 18 August update says several tracks near Transmission Gully are closed Monday to Saturday while restoration work continues, but are open on Sundays. 18 Aug 2026. Source
  3. (Privacy) Coles and Woolworths are testing facial recognition in stores. Both major Australian supermarket groups confirmed trials of facial-recognition technology, while Australia’s privacy regulator has recently reiterated that biometric collection in high-volume retail settings faces a high legal bar. 17–18 Aug 2026. Source Regulator
  4. Face- and palm-payment terminals are being introduced in Australia and New Zealand. Verifone’s Victa terminals are rolling out with hardware capable of biometric payments and age verification; the biometric functions are expected to become available progressively as merchants and users opt in. 12–13 Aug 2026. Source
  5. New testing changed the practical risk picture for recalled asbestos-contaminated play sand. Independent testing reported by the Guardian found respirable asbestos fibres were released during ordinary handling in most tested samples, after earlier recall messaging had described risk as low unless the sand was mechanically processed. 9 Aug 2026. Source
  6. Air New Zealand and Air Chathams expanded through-ticket regional connections. From 13 August their interline partnership expanded to Auckland–Whanganui, Auckland–Chatham Islands, Wellington–Chatham Islands and Christchurch–Chatham Islands, allowing more journeys to be booked as connected itineraries. 13 Aug 2026. Source
  7. Shanghai–Auckland–Buenos Aires flights double in December. China Eastern will increase the service from two to four flights a week from December 2026, materially increasing New Zealand’s direct one-stop air link to South America. 24 Jun 2026 announcement. Source
  8. New Zealand’s WoF schedule changes from 1 November. New light vehicles will get four years before their second WoF; many 4–14-year-old light vehicles will progressively move to two-yearly inspections; older pre-2000 light vehicles and motorcycles move from six-monthly to annual inspections; and light rental vehicles move to annual CoF A inspections. 1 Nov 2026 start. Source
  9. Visitors will get less time to drive on overseas car licences. From 1 November, the maximum period for driving in New Zealand on a valid overseas car licence falls from 18 months to 12 months from the day of last arrival; truck and motorcycle limits remain 12 months. 1 Nov 2026 start. Source
  10. New Skilled Migrant residence settings start on 24 August. Immigration New Zealand’s finalised changes update wage-threshold treatment and qualification evidence for the Skilled Migrant Category and work-to-residence pathways, including removal of the 120-credit requirement for overseas Trade and Technician qualifications. 24 Aug 2026 start. Source
  11. Children-on-footpaths and e-scooter cycle-lane rule changes have been confirmed. The Government confirmed a transport-rule package that will allow children aged 12 and under to ride bicycles on footpaths with an accompanying older rider and allow e-scooters in cycle lanes. 2 Jul 2026 confirmation. Source
  12. Class 1 licence holders can now drive heavier zero-emission vehicles. From 6 August, Class 1 holders can drive qualifying zero-emission heavy vehicles up to 7,500kg, and Class 2 holders can drive qualifying low- or zero-emission rigid buses up to 22,000kg. 6 Aug 2026. Source
  13. Total Mobility’s nationwide subsidy is now 65%, with the review completed. The fare subsidy reduced from 75% to 65% from 1 July, and the August review outcome confirms further work on national consistency, wheelchair-accessible vehicles and public-transport discounts. 7–9 Aug 2026 review update. Source
  14. Eli Lilly opened limited early access to retatrutide for severe refractory obesity. Lilly’s expanded-access programme allows a narrow group of adults with refractory obesity plus at least two serious obesity-related conditions, who cannot join relevant trials, to seek access before FDA approval. 3 Aug 2026. Source
  15. (Longevity) Caloric restriction slowed several organ-specific biological-age measures in a randomized trial. In a CALERIE analysis of 185 participants followed for up to two years, caloric restriction produced the clearest differences in metabolic, cardiovascular, immune and whole-body biological-age measures; kidney age was unaffected. These are biomarker results, not evidence of longer human lifespan. May 2026 publication. Source
  16. (Australia) PBS advisers recommended broader funding for triptorelin. Australia’s Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee recommended extending subsidised access to triptorelin for breast cancer, endometriosis and gender dysphoria after the planned withdrawal of Zoladex created a treatment-access gap; implementation would require government action. 18 Aug 2026. Source
  17. (Australia) The NDIS reform bill passed the House after substantial amendments. The House of Representatives passed the bill on 19 August after 63 amendments, moving a major redesign of disability-support rules further through Parliament. 19 Aug 2026. Source
  18. (Australia) Gambling-ad reforms include a national opt-out register. The federal reform package includes a single-service register allowing people to opt out of gambling advertising, alongside restrictions on inducements and agent commissions; the bill was being progressed through Parliament this week. 18 Aug 2026. Source

item.title: Leave Rules Reset as Travel and Privacy Shift
item.description: New leave law, privacy breach, licence changes, travel options and practical health updates lead this briefing.
item.content:encoded:
A new employment-leave law leads a practical briefing spanning privacy, transport, travel, health, consumer costs and Australian work conditions.

  1. New Zealand has enacted a replacement for the Holidays Act. The Employment Leave Act 2026 received Royal assent on 6 August and is scheduled to replace the Holidays Act on 6 August 2028. Annual and sick leave will accrue in hours from the first day of employment; additional or casual hours can instead attract 12.5% upfront leave compensation, and leave can be taken in part-days. 6 Aug 2026. Source
  2. (Privacy) Quest Apartment Hotels disclosed a customer-data breach. Quest says unauthorised access through a third-party vulnerability exposed customer records created before June 2025, including names, email and street addresses and, for some people, dates of birth; affected customers are being notified. 18 Aug 2026. Source
  3. New Zealand's car-licence process changes in January. From 25 January 2027 the full-licence practical test is removed, eyesight checks are no longer required when applying for restricted or full licences, the full-licence application fee falls to NZ$25.90, and minimum learner and restricted periods change for drivers under 25. 25 Jan 2027 effective date. Source
  4. Auckland's City Rail Link opens on 13 September. The confirmed opening date brings the new underground rail link and its central-city stations into passenger service next month, materially changing rail trips through central Auckland. 13 Sep 2026 opening. Source
  5. Jetstar put Wellington–Gold Coast fares into a large sale. Jetstar released 225,000 discounted domestic and international fares on 19 August, including Gold Coast–Wellington from A$197 one way; the public sale runs to 24 August unless sold out, with eligible travel dates extending into June 2027. 19 Aug 2026. Source
  6. 2degrees raised prices on several broadband plans. From 14 August, Unlimited and Ultimate Unlimited fibre plans increased by NZ$2 a month and copper broadband increased by NZ$4 a month for affected customers. 14 Aug 2026. Source
  7. Trade Me removed seller Success Fees but added buyer fees. Since 10 March, casual Marketplace sellers no longer pay the 7.9% Success Fee; Ping seller transaction fees are 2.19%, bank transfer has been removed as a payment option, and buyers pay a service fee on purchases above NZ$20, rising by transaction value. 10 Mar 2026. Source
  8. Most stable long-term prescriptions can now cover 12 months. Since 1 February, New Zealand prescribers can issue prescriptions for up to 12 months for many people with stable long-term conditions, while still choosing a shorter duration when clinically appropriate. 1 Feb 2026. Source
  9. Participating pharmacies can directly supply more funded medicines. From 2 June, pharmacies using the Extended Pharmacy Services framework can supply specified funded medicines without a prescription to eligible people, including some common pain relief and oral-rehydration products, under the service's eligibility rules. 2 Jun 2026. Source
  10. Six toy sets were recalled over choking risk. Product Safety New Zealand posted recalls on 13 August for six toy sets sold through Dollarama Rolleston and Nothing Over $3 after they failed the mandatory toy standard for small parts; consumers are told to stop using them and return them for a full refund. 13 Aug 2026. Source
  11. (Australia) Payday Super is now in force. From 1 July, Australian employers generally must pay superannuation at the same time as salary or wages, with contributions required to reach the employee's nominated super account within seven business days. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  12. (Australia) Paid parental leave expanded to 26 weeks. For children born or adopted from 1 July 2026, eligible families can receive up to 130 days, or 26 weeks, of Parental Leave Pay; the current weekly rate is A$1,004.70. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  13. (Australia) Western Sydney gets direct Vietnam flights in January. Vietjet will begin Western Sydney International–Ho Chi Minh City flights twice weekly in January 2027 and increase to three weekly services in March, adding another direct Australia–Vietnam option from the new airport. 10 Aug 2026 ticket-sale update. Source
  14. (NZ Tenancy) Residential property managers face a new regulatory regime. The Government has announced a proposed light-touch regime requiring residential property managers and organisations to meet conduct and accountability requirements; legislation is planned rather than yet in force. 24 Mar 2026. Source
  15. (Finance) ANZ changed floating mortgage and savings rates. ANZ New Zealand raised its Floating Home Loan rate to 6.04% and Flexible Home Loan rate to 6.15% from 29 July, both up 0.25 percentage points, and lifted the Serious Saver premium rate by 0.25 points from 1 August for a total 1.80% when conditions are met. 29 Jul–1 Aug 2026. Source
  16. Employment Relations Act changes are already in effect. Since 21 February, new employees no longer automatically spend their first 30 days on collective-agreement terms; a statutory contractor gateway test applies, and new employment agreements above the NZ$200,000 remuneration threshold have different unjustified-dismissal rules, with transitional arrangements for existing agreements. 21 Feb 2026. Source
  17. Some Coversyl users need a new prescription during the brand change. The existing Coversyl range is being replaced by perindopril arginine strengths; people taking the old 2mg or 8mg tablets need a new prescription from early September, while the 4mg transition follows in October. 30 Jul 2026 update. Source
  18. (Wellington) LEGO Star Wars exhibition is now open at Tākina. The New Zealand-exclusive LEGO Star Wars exhibition is running at Tākina with large-scale Star Wars builds and timed sessions, including August and September dates now on sale. 27 Jun 2026 opening. Source

item.title: Security Fixes, Cheaper Australia and New Digital Choices
item.description: Security fixes, lower Australia travel costs, Melbourne Fabric demand and practical software changes lead this briefing.
item.content:encoded:
Security, software, travel and service changes dominate this briefing, alongside new choices in Australia, Wellington and DRM-free gaming.

  1. iOS 26.6.1 and iPadOS 26.6.1 patch major vulnerabilities. Apple released the updates for supported devices with fixes across Audio, ImageIO, IOGPUFamily, Kernel, Telephony and WebKit, addressing flaws associated with data exposure, crashes, memory corruption, arbitrary code execution and network-traffic interception. 17 Aug 2026. Source
  2. (Australia) Qantas launched its biggest domestic sale of 2026. More than two million discounted economy and business seats are on sale across 101 routes and 60 destinations, with economy fares from A$99 one way and travel dates extending through August 2027; the sale ends 25 August unless sold out earlier. 18 Aug 2026. Source
  3. (Melbourne Fabric) Multiple strong Fabric roles are live at once. SEEK currently shows about 60 Microsoft Fabric listings across Melbourne, including an enterprise Data & AI project manager, Melbourne Business School enterprise-applications role, a Fabric data-engineering lead for a major financial-services transformation and a A$180,000 technical delivery lead explicitly owning a Fabric platform. 18 Aug 2026, current listings. Source
  4. Google unveiled the Pixel 11 phone family. The Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL and 11 Pro Fold were announced with Tensor G6 processors, upgraded cameras and Qi2.2 wireless charging; the phones are scheduled to ship from 20 August. 12 Aug 2026. Source
  5. Microsoft 365 feature updates are ending on Windows 10. Current Channel Microsoft 365 Apps on Windows 10 stop receiving new features after Version 2608 in August; the apps remain on Version 2608 with security updates through 10 October 2028, while later enterprise channels reach the same feature cutoff in October 2026 or January 2027. Aug 2026. Source
  6. (Privacy) NZ indirect data collection now usually requires notice. Information Privacy Principle 3A has been in force since 1 May, requiring agencies that collect a person’s information from another source to take reasonable steps to notify that person, subject to the Act’s exceptions. 1 May 2026. Source
  7. (Privacy) Chrome is suppressing billions of malicious Android notifications. Google says its current defenses revoke notification permissions from inactive or suspicious sites, detect coordinated malicious service-worker behavior, rate-limit disruptive domains through Firebase Cloud Messaging and expose easier notification controls on Android; it reports roughly seven billion malicious or unwanted notifications blocked per day. 13 Aug 2026. Source
  8. WhatsApp now supports standalone iPad registration and richer car use. Users can register an account directly on iPad without linking a phone; refreshed CarPlay and Android Auto support messages, calls, call history and favourites, while web and desktop can open and annotate PDFs in-chat. 22 Jul 2026. Source
  9. OneDrive can move local folders from File Explorer. The Windows deferred ring reached its 3 August target for a OneDrive version that adds a right-click “Move to OneDrive” command for local folders, making backup and sync available directly from File Explorer. 3 Aug 2026. Source
  10. (Australia) Revolut is now a licensed Australian bank. Revolut received a full unrestricted Australian ADI licence and launched Revolut Bank Australia, adding Instant Access Savings and credit cards; eligible deposits are covered by the Financial Claims Scheme up to A$250,000 per account holder. 21–22 Jul 2026. Source
  11. Spark raised prices on several Pay Monthly mobile plans. From 31 July, existing and new customers on affected plans saw monthly increases of NZ$2 on the 3GB plan, NZ$5 on the 6GB plan with an extra 2GB of data, NZ$3 on the 75GB and 150GB plans, and NZ$5 on Unlimited and Unlimited Netflix plans. 31 Jul 2026. Source
  12. (Longevity) NR and HIIT shifted muscle epigenetic clocks differently. Across three human studies, five months of nicotinamide riboside was associated with lower skeletal-muscle epigenetic age acceleration on several clocks, while four to six weeks of high-intensity interval training moved some clocks in the opposite direction; these are biomarker findings and do not show longer lifespan. Aug 2026 issue. Source
  13. (Wellington) Te Papa opens a major Māori carving exhibition. He Toi Whakairo opens 29 August with 147 carvings spanning seven centuries, many never publicly exhibited before; the free long-term exhibition is scheduled to run until August 2031. 29 Aug 2026 opening. Source
  14. (Gaming) Two Star Ocean games are now DRM-free on GOG. Star Ocean The Divine Force and Star Ocean The Second Story R launched on GOG without DRM and joined the GOG Preservation Program, which commits the storefront to maintaining compatibility on modern systems. 28 Jul 2026. Source
  15. Spark is moving customers to a new voicemail service. Migrations run from 24 August to near the end of October; once migrated, customers can use the Spark Voicemail app for message lists, transcriptions, multiple greetings and sharing, free on Pay Monthly or as a NZ$1 monthly extra on Prepaid. 24 Aug 2026 start. Source
  16. ANZ Direct Auth no longer supports iOS 15. Since 3 August, ANZ Direct Auth requires iOS 16 or later; older devices that cannot upgrade, including iPhone 6, first-generation iPhone SE and iPhone 7 models, require a newer device to continue using the authentication app. 3 Aug 2026. Source
  17. Firefox is moving from four-week to two-week releases. Mozilla says the transition begins with Firefox 155 Beta, after which Nightly, Beta and Release periods on desktop and Android will each run for two weeks rather than four. 23 Jul 2026 announcement. Source
  18. Edge switches to two-week Stable releases on 27 August. Starting with Edge 152, the normal Stable channel moves from monthly to two-week major releases; managed organizations can retain the eight-week Extended Stable channel. 27 Aug 2026 start. Source

item.title: Zip Exits as Digital Services and Privacy Expand
item.description: Fresh practical changes cover payments, renting, connectivity, privacy, Android, travel and Australian work conditions.
item.content:encoded:
A second pass through the wider news landscape found a different set of practical changes, led by a New Zealand finance exit, fully digital rental bonds, new connectivity and privacy tools, and useful travel and Australian employment changes.

  1. Zip Pay in 4 has stopped accepting new NZ purchases. From 17 August, New Zealand Zip customers can no longer make new Pay in 4 purchases after spending limits were reduced to zero; existing balances and scheduled repayments continue until they are cleared. 17 Aug 2026. Source
  2. (NZ Tenancy) Rental bond transactions are now fully digital. Since 29 June, bond lodgements, top-ups, refunds and changes of tenant or landlord are handled through Bond Hub or connected property-management software; paper forms for those transactions are no longer accepted, and tenants can see bond records and receive status updates digitally. 29 Jun 2026. Source
  3. Consumer NZ has launched a flight-complaints portal. Consumer NZ launched a dedicated flight complaints portal and information hub for New Zealand travellers, providing a single place to work through airline complaint options and passenger-rights information when flights go wrong. 3 Jul 2026. Source
  4. One NZ Satellite now carries apps and calls. Eligible One NZ customers outside cell-tower coverage can use selected apps over satellite, including WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Google Maps, AccuWeather and NZTopo50; supported phones can also send attachments and make WhatsApp calls where there is a clear view of the sky. 18 Aug 2026, current service status. Source
  5. Kiwibank has enabled open banking across its digital channels. Individual and business customers can now authorise supported third parties to initiate payments or access permitted account information through either the Kiwibank app or internet banking, with authorisations viewable and revocable by the customer. 28 May 2026. Source
  6. Spark offers verified caller identification for its own calls. Spark customers can opt into Verified Call in the Spark app so genuine calls from Spark display its name, logo, verification badge and reason for calling instead of appearing as an ordinary unidentified call. 18 Aug 2026, current service status. Source
  7. Signal can now link another Android phone or tablet. Signal Android 8.20 adds linked Android phones and tablets, while iOS 8.22 expands linked-device support to iPhones; a new linked device can optionally receive the full message history plus the last 45 days of saved media through an end-to-end encrypted transfer. 4 Aug 2026. Source
  8. Android 17 is available on supported Pixel devices. Google released Android 17 on 16 June, bringing the new platform release to most supported Pixels with new privacy, security, large-screen, media and performance changes rather than leaving the update in beta. 16 Jun 2026. Source
  9. ChatGPT desktop now carries Projects and Work across devices. OpenAI’s July desktop update added Projects to the Windows and macOS apps, unified Chat and Work recents, and lets cloud Work conversations continue across devices; a separate global search update also made chats, projects, images and documents searchable from one place. 14–16 Jul 2026. Source
  10. Android Quick Share now works directly with iPhone AirDrop. On supported Android models, Quick Share can send files to nearby iPhones through AirDrop and receive AirDrop transfers back, removing the need for a separate cross-platform transfer app for supported devices. 18 Aug 2026, current service status. Source
  11. (Privacy) Firefox’s free built-in VPN is rolling out on Android in NZ. Mozilla began the Android rollout on 28 July in New Zealand and other supported countries, bringing Firefox’s built-in VPN from desktop to mobile so browsing can be routed through the browser’s VPN without installing a separate VPN app. 28 Jul 2026. Source
  12. (Privacy) Firefox extensions lost automatic local-file access. Firefox 153 separates access to local file URLs from general website permissions. The new “Access local files on your computer” permission is off by default for every extension, including already-installed extensions, until the user explicitly enables it. 23 Jul 2026. Source
  13. (Australia) Minimum award wages rose 4.75%. From the first full pay period on or after 1 July, Australia’s National Minimum Wage is A$26.44 an hour or A$1,004.90 a week, while minimum award wages increased 4.75%, changing the statutory pay floor for most Australian employees. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  14. (Crypto) Australia’s expanded crypto transfer rules are active. From 1 July, AML/CTF obligations that had been deferred for newly regulated virtual-asset services began applying, including customer due diligence, reporting, record-keeping and travel-rule requirements for relevant virtual-asset transfers. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  15. Virgin Australia Flex fares now include free Fly Ahead. Eligible domestic Economy Flex passengers can use the Virgin Australia app to move to an available earlier flight on the same day without a change fee or fare difference, extending the feature beyond high-tier frequent flyers. 2 Jul 2026. Source
  16. Queenstown–Brisbane now has a direct seasonal Air NZ service. Air New Zealand launched the route on 22 June and is operating three flights a week through 23 October, adding 16,500 seats and another direct New Zealand–Queensland option. 1 Jul 2026 update. Source
  17. (Longevity) PAI-1 inhibitor trial shifted multiple aging biomarkers. In an open-label trial, 19 evaluable adults aged 50–75 took TM5614 for four months; two DNA-methylation clocks fell by roughly two to three years on average alongside changes in proteins, immune cells and other aging-related markers. The small uncontrolled study does not establish that the drug extends lifespan or healthspan. 16 Jun 2026. Source
  18. (NZ Tenancy) New meth-contamination thresholds now govern rentals. Since 16 April, New Zealand rental properties are legally considered contaminated above 15µg/100cm² of meth residue in affected areas and uninhabitable above 30µg/100cm², with testing and decontamination tied to the specified NZ standard and shorter termination rights possible for uninhabitable homes. 16 Apr 2026. Source

item.title: KiwiSaver Rises as Privacy and Travel Options Shift
item.description: New Zealand saving, government access and crypto reporting changes lead a briefing with privacy upgrades, Australian consumer reforms and new flight options.
item.content:encoded:
Concrete changes to saving, digital services, privacy, consumer rights and travel make up today’s briefing, with 19 developments that passed the relevance and factual filters.

  1. KiwiSaver default contributions are now 3.5%. Since 1 April, employees contributing at the default rate have 3.5% deducted and the compulsory matching employer rate is also 3.5%; employees can apply for a temporary reduction to 3%, and the default rises again to 4% in 2028. 19 Mar 2026. Source
  2. The Govt.nz app now includes its digital-wallet foundation. The current second release lets New Zealanders set up a wallet for accredited digital credentials, pin government services and receive location-based emergency updates; the first credentials are expected to become available progressively from late August. 18 Aug 2026, current service status. Source
  3. (Crypto/Privacy) New Zealand crypto reporting is active. From 1 April, New Zealand-based Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers must collect identifying and tax-residency information about users and detailed information on relevant transactions, report annually, and retain records for seven years; Inland Revenue will also exchange CARF information internationally. 1 Apr 2026. Source
  4. (Australia) Subscription traps and unfair trading will be banned. Australia’s Parliament passed the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Unfair Trading Practices) Bill on 2 July; the new prohibitions on unfair trading practices and subscription traps are scheduled to apply from 1 July 2027. 2 Jul 2026. Source
  5. (Australia) Victoria adds more renter protections in October. From 13 October, rental providers must give advance notice and evidence for bond claims, keep minimum-standard compliance records, arrange gas and electrical safety checks every two years for all rental agreements, and comply with other new rental-law requirements. 13 Oct 2026 effective date. Source
  6. (Australia) NSW Smart Rental Bonds start rolling out this month. Parramatta, the Central Coast and Penrith are the first areas in a phased August rollout allowing eligible renters to digitally transfer an existing bond to a new NSW rental rather than funding another full bond during the move. 8 Jul 2026 announcement. Source
  7. New Zealand consumer-credit regulation has moved to the FMA. Since 1 July, the Financial Markets Authority has regulated the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act, taken over active investigations and most litigation, and become the contact point for consumers and lenders on CCCFA matters and relevant fair-dealing breaches. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  8. (Privacy) Chrome Android can share approximate location. Chrome on Android now lets users give a website approximate rather than precise location when exact coordinates are unnecessary, while retaining the option to share precise location for services such as navigation. 5 May 2026. Source
  9. (Privacy) Cross-platform RCS gains end-to-end encryption. End-to-end encrypted RCS is rolling out in beta for iPhones running iOS 26.5 with supported carriers and Android phones using the latest Google Messages; encrypted conversations show a lock icon and the feature is on by default where supported. 12 May 2026. Source
  10. (Privacy) Firefox 153 adds native Containers in preview. Firefox now has a built-in Containers preview that can separate work, shopping, personal and banking sessions in one browser while isolating cookies and ad tracking between containers, without requiring the older Multi-Account Containers extension for the core feature. 21 Jul 2026. Source
  11. Chrome mobile can autofill passport and licence details. Advanced autofill is now available on iOS and Android for complex information such as flight and vehicle details, and can use passport, driver-licence and Known Traveler Number data stored in Google Wallet with explicit user permission. 23 Jun 2026. Source
  12. Gemini in Chrome is available in New Zealand. Google expanded Gemini in Chrome to New Zealand on desktop and iOS, including help inside the current tab, multi-tab comparison, integrations with Gmail, Maps, Calendar and YouTube, and image transformation from the browser side panel. 11 Mar 2026. Source
  13. Chrome adds vertical tabs and full-page reading mode. Chrome’s rollout lets users move tabs to a vertical side panel and open webpages in a distraction-reduced full-page reading interface directly from the browser. 7 Apr 2026. Source
  14. (Australia) Auckland–Western Sydney flights start 26 October. Air New Zealand will operate three return services a week between Auckland and the new Western Sydney International Airport on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, adding a second Sydney airport option. 17 Jul 2026 update. Source
  15. Christchurch gets three new long-haul Air New Zealand routes. Non-stop Christchurch–Singapore begins 28 October, Christchurch–Tokyo Narita on 28 November, and Christchurch–Perth on 30 November, giving South Island travellers three additional direct international options. 20 May 2026. Source
  16. Auckland–Port Moresby direct flights return in November. Air Niugini will launch three non-stop Auckland–Port Moresby services a week from 17 November, restoring the direct link after 26 years and timing services for onward connections to several Asian destinations. 17 Jul 2026. Source
  17. Jetstar restores Sydney–Christchurch in October. Jetstar will resume the route from 26 October with four weekly flights on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday. 25 Jun 2026. Source
  18. Auckland–Sunshine Coast loses Jetstar service from 24 October. Jetstar is suspending its direct Auckland–Sunshine Coast route from 24 October; Air New Zealand’s seasonal service remains a separate option. 20 Jul 2026. Source
  19. (Australia/Crypto) Australia has enacted a digital-assets framework. The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 received assent on 8 April and creates a Corporations Act framework for digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms, including Australian financial-services licensing provisions; the substantive framework is scheduled to commence on 8 April 2027. 8 Apr 2026. Source

item.title: Safer Messaging, Stable GP Fees and Better Travel
item.description: Fresh changes span Windows, GP and medicine access, privacy controls, travel options and Wellington hiking.
item.content:encoded:
Practical changes dominate this briefing, from frozen GP fees and wider medicine access to browser controls, safer messaging and easier travel and renting.

  1. GP consultation fees frozen for 2026/27. From 1 July, standard GP consultation fees are held at their 8 June 2026 levels, with a zero allowable increase across all age groups unless Health New Zealand approves a specific exception. That makes the current fee level the baseline for the full funding year rather than allowing the usual annual rise. 23 Jul 2026. Source
  2. (Privacy) WhatsApp adds on-device Scam Alert. WhatsApp is testing an optional Scam Alert that uses on-device machine learning to flag likely scam messages. Classification stays on the device; nothing is automatically reported, and users choose whether to block, report, continue, or optionally share the last five received messages to improve detection. 13 Aug 2026. Source
  3. Windows 11 gets a substantial August feature update. The August security update is rolling out support for Windows Hello Enhanced Sign-in Security with external fingerprint sensors, the ability to uninstall the Image Generation AI model on Copilot+ PCs, better typo-tolerant Windows Search, middle-click folder opening in new tabs, touchpad customisation and other usability changes. 11 Aug 2026. Source
  4. (Australia) Victoria launches portable rental bonds. Eligible Victorian renters can now transfer an existing bond to a new rental instead of funding two bonds during a move. The scheme is optional, costs A$25 to use, and renters pay only the difference if the new bond is higher. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  5. (Australia) Digital arrival cards are going nationwide. Australia will roll out the Australia Travel Declaration to all international airports and seaports before the end of 2027, progressively replacing the paper incoming passenger card. The current Qantas pilot lets passengers pre-fill the digital declaration up to 72 hours before arrival, with more capital-city airports joining before the end of 2026. 13 Jul 2026. Source
  6. Skin-cancer care is expanding into GP clinics. New Zealand is moving more assessment and removal of suspicious skin spots and moles into local GP and community clinics as the first stage of a NZ$23 million community-care investment, reducing reliance on hospital or private treatment pathways. 1 Aug 2026. Source
  7. (Privacy) Full uBlock Origin is leaving Microsoft Edge. Microsoft has set the consumer transition away from Manifest V2 extensions to finish by the end of 2026, with notices and gradual disabling beginning this month. Full uBlock Origin depends on MV2; uBlock Origin Lite remains available under MV3, while Firefox and Brave continue to support the full extension. 10 Aug 2026. Source
  8. ANZ changes term-deposit withdrawal rules. ANZ New Zealand’s updated general terms took effect on 10 August. They clarify that cancelling during a cooling-off period can reduce earned interest, and that early-withdrawal proceeds may be paid on the 32nd day after the request, or the next business day when applicable. 10 Aug 2026. Source
  9. New Zealand’s faster medicine-approval pathway is active. Medsafe can now use its verification pathway for medicines already approved by two recognised overseas regulators, focusing its assessment on verifying those approvals and New Zealand-specific factors instead of repeating the full evaluation. Recognised regulators include Australia, the US, Canada, UK, EU, Singapore and Switzerland. 3 Jul 2026. Source
  10. Oestradiol patches become easier to collect. From 1 August, people using funded Estradiol TDP Mylan patches can collect up to three months at once and are no longer subject to the two-patch dispensing limit. Estradot arrangements remain unchanged because of continuing global supply constraints. 1 Aug 2026. Source
  11. Rural emergency teams gain easier access to critical medicines. From 1 July, PRIME services can obtain a broader range of funded emergency medicines through Practitioner Supply Orders, and tenecteplase is funded for eligible pre-hospital heart-attack treatment by PRIME and ambulance services. The change particularly matters when patients are more than 90 minutes from hospital treatment. 1 Jul 2026. Source
  12. Rosuvastatin access opens from October. Pharmac will remove Special Authority and hospital restrictions from all funded rosuvastatin tablet strengths on 1 October 2026. Pharmac estimates around 81,000 additional people could access the cholesterol-lowering medicine in the first year after restrictions are removed. 30 Jun 2026. Source
  13. Microsoft is merging its two Copilot app experiences. Microsoft has begun the worldwide mobile and web rollout of a unified Microsoft Copilot app combining consumer Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot access under one interface while keeping personal and work data separated. Windows and Mac rollout follows in mid-September. 13 Aug 2026. Source
  14. Brave Containers isolate accounts without separate profiles. Brave 1.92 adds built-in Containers on desktop, separating cookies and site storage between container tabs. That allows work and personal accounts, admin and normal accounts, or multiple sessions of the same service to coexist in one browser window without sharing their stored site data. 2 Jul 2026. Source
  15. Qantas restores direct Auckland–Gold Coast flights. Qantas is now operating the Auckland–Gold Coast route three times weekly on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, with Economy, Economy Plus and Business cabins. The restored service gives New Zealand travellers another direct carrier and the route’s only Business cabin. 29 Jun 2026. Source
  16. Air New Zealand Skynest is bookable. Economy and Premium Economy passengers can now book a four-hour session in one of six lie-flat Skynest pods on selected Auckland–New York flights. Air New Zealand’s current booking page lists travel from late December 2026, with sessions sold as an add-on to a normal seat. 16 Aug 2026, current booking status. Source
  17. (Longevity) Vegan diet shifts aging-related epigenetic markers. In a randomized one-month trial of 48 healthy adults, a vegan diet changed DNA-methylation patterns linked to inflammation, immune regulation and metabolism compared with a meat-rich diet. Two biological-aging clocks showed a short-term deceleration signal; this is a biomarker finding, not evidence that the diet extends human lifespan. 4 Aug 2026. Source
  18. (Wellington hiking) More Belmont tracks have reopened. Greater Wellington’s 30 July update says several tracks affected by Transmission Gully restoration work have reopened and most of Belmont Regional Park is now accessible seven days a week. Remaining weekday restrictions are concentrated around Cannons Head and limited worksite sections, which are open on Sundays. 30 Jul 2026. Source
